Samantha —

Really appreciate the screenshot — that made the issue clear. This is (unfortunately) a common Google Calendar forwarding quirk: when an invite is forwarded between calendars with different defaults, the TZID can be lost and the event becomes 'floating' relative to the recipient's calendar. Two quick fixes that have worked for customers:

1) I just created and sent a new invite where the event is explicitly set to TZID:Australia/Sydney. That invite also includes the meeting link and a short join section in the body so if the event time appears off someone can still join the right link. I've attached demo-join-info.ics — please ask your admin to import it if forward/import is more reliable for your team.

2) If someone sees a wrong time after receiving an invite, have them open the event and check the event's time zone field (not their calendar default). If it shows "(floating)" or no TZID, they can edit the event and set the zone to Australia/Sydney and the time will adjust correctly.

To keep things simple we will plan for Option A: Thu Mar 20, 09:00 Australia/Sydney (AEDT). If that works for you I'll mark the opportunity in our CRM (deal RWD-4321) and send a calendar reminder 24 hours before.
